requirements: Navigate the maze from S (start) to E (exit) using only single-step moves: Up, Down, Left, Right.
Collect the key (K) before passing through the locked door (D).
Avoid walls (#) and handle traps (T), which impose a 5-move penalty when entered.

Maintain a persistent internal knowledge base covering: visited cells, blocked cells, successful moves, failed moves, dead ends, trap/key/door locations, successful and failed strategies, and mistakes with their causes.
Avoid repeating actions already learned to be unsuccessful.
Operate within the limited number of moves allowed per episode.
Devise an original strategy since the solution path is never provided.
Interact one action at a time using the move tool and process feedback after each action.
success_criteria: Agent reaches the exit E from the start S within the episode move limit.
Key K is collected before any traversal of door D.
Internal knowledge base accurately reflects the discovered maze layout, hazards, and failed/successful actions.
Learned-unsuccessful actions (e.g., moving into walls, re-entering traps) are not repeated.
Demonstrated persistent learning: improved efficiency (fewer wasted moves/penalties) over time or across episodes.
Traps are recorded when discovered and avoided thereafter to minimize the 5-move penalties.
known_info: Cell symbols: S = start, E = exit, . = open cell, # = wall, K = key, D = locked door, T = trap.
Movement allowed only Up, Down, Left, Right; diagonals are not allowed.
Walls (#) block movement entirely; the locked door (D) requires the key (K); entering a trap adds a 5-move penalty.
The agent receives feedback from the environment after every action.
The agent starts at S and initially knows the rules but not the maze layout.
The number of moves per episode is limited (exact value not given).
Tool semantics: 'Right' increases x, 'Left' decreases x, 'Up' increases y, 'Down' decreases y.
The solution path is never provided; the agent must create its own strategy.
unknown_info: The actual maze layout per episode: positions of walls, open cells, key, door, traps, start, and exit.
Which maze size (5x5, 6x6, or 7x7) applies in a given episode.
The exact numeric move limit per episode.
Whether the trap's 5-move penalty is deducted from the move budget and exactly how it is applied.
The exact format and content of the environment feedback returned after each action.
Whether the maze layout persists across episodes or whether 'persistent' refers only to the agent's accumulated knowledge.
Whether multiple keys or doors exist and whether the door is mandatory on the path to the exit.
Initial absolute coordinates of S and the coordinate origin of the grid.
constraints: Only four movement actions are permitted (Up/Down/Left/Right); no diagonal movement.
The agent cannot move through walls (#).
The door (D) cannot be passed until the key (K) is collected.
A limited number of moves is available per episode; traps consume an additional 5 moves.
Actions are taken one at a time; no multi-step command batches.
The solution path is never provided.
The agent must maintain persistent knowledge of the specified categories (visited, blocked, moves, dead ends, traps, keys, doors, strategies, mistakes).
The agent must not repeat actions it has learned are unsuccessful.
available_actions: Call move with direction 'Up', 'Down', 'Left', or 'Right' to move one cell on the grid.
Observe environment feedback after every action.
Update the internal knowledge base with newly discovered maze information (visited cells, blocked cells, hazards, etc.).
Record successful and failed strategies, environmental patterns, hazards, exploration techniques, and mistakes with their causes.
Select the next move based on accumulated knowledge, avoiding known-failed actions.
expected_challenges: Exploration vs. limited move budget tradeoff: the layout is unknown, so systematic exploration may exhaust the move limit.
Key-door dependency: the door may block the route to the exit, requiring the key to be found first without knowing either location.
Trap avoidance without prior knowledge: trap locations can only be learned by (risking) encounter, each mistake costing 5 moves.
Efficient dead-end detection and backtracking without re-treading failed paths or looping.
Maintaining consistent, accurate, persistent memory across actions and possibly episodes.
Avoiding repeated failed moves when the same wall or blocked edge is encountered again.
Environmental ambiguity: feedback format, move-limit value, and persistence semantics are unspecified and must be inferred from interaction.
